item.content:encoded:
On this page you will find an ideal student paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end.

An Ideal Student Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

An ideal student is a student who treats education as a responsibility, not only as a race for marks. He attends classes regularly, listens to his teachers carefully, and asks questions when he does not understand a lesson. He studies every day, reviews his lessons before they are forgotten, and tries to understand ideas instead of memorising them without meaning.

An ideal student is also good in character. He respects his parents, teachers, and classmates, and follows the rules of his school. He is truthful, punctual, and helpful, and he admits his mistakes honestly. He keeps his body healthy through exercise, sleep, and play, because a healthy body helps concentration.

He does not become proud after success or hopeless after failure. He helps weaker classmates, keeps his notes organised, and uses his time well. In this way, he prepares himself not only for examinations but also for a useful life.

An Ideal Student Paragraph in 250 Words

Best for Class 8–10 and SSC.

An ideal student is a student who treats education as a responsibility rather than a race for marks. Such a learner attends classes regularly, listens carefully, asks questions, and reviews lessons before they are forgotten. Instead of memorising every sentence, the student tries to understand ideas and explain them independently. He keeps a daily routine for study, revision, and rest, and he completes his homework and classwork on time. He prepares his lessons before class so that he can follow the teacher easily and take part in discussion.

Good study is balanced with good character. An ideal student respects parents, teachers, classmates, and school rules. The student is truthful, punctual, helpful, and willing to admit mistakes. He never copies in examinations and never looks down on weaker students. He avoids gossip and useless activities in his free time. Instead, he helps his classmates, shares his notes, and learns from group study. Exercise, sleep, and recreation are also important because a healthy body supports concentration and a fresh mind learns faster.

An excellent learner does not become proud after success or discouraged after failure. He finds out why he failed, corrects his weakness, and tries again with more care. He uses technology responsibly, for learning and research, not for wasting time. He also takes part in social service and school activities when he gets time. These habits prepare a person not only for examinations but also for useful citizenship. True excellence combines knowledge, discipline, kindness, and the courage to keep improving.

An Ideal Student Paragraph in 300 Words

Best for SSC and HSC.

An ideal student is one who treats education as a responsibility rather than a race for marks. He understands that student life is the best time to build knowledge, character, and good habits for the future. So he attends classes regularly, listens to his teachers with attention, and asks questions whenever he does not understand a lesson. He studies every day according to a routine, reviews his lessons before they are forgotten, and completes his homework on time. Instead of memorising every sentence without meaning, he tries to understand ideas deeply and explain them in his own words. He keeps his notes organised and reads reference books.

But good marks alone do not make an ideal student. Character matters just as much as study. An ideal student respects his parents, teachers, and classmates, and he follows the rules of his school and society. He is truthful, punctual, honest, and helpful. He admits his mistakes, keeps his promises, and never cheats in examinations. He is kind to weaker classmates and learns from others without pride. He keeps his body healthy through regular exercise, enough sleep, and outdoor games, because a healthy body supports a fresh and attentive mind.

An ideal student also knows how to face both success and failure. Success does not make him proud, and failure does not make him hopeless. When he fails, he finds the reason, corrects his weakness, and works harder the next time. He uses mobile phones and the internet responsibly, mainly for learning, and avoids wasting hours on useless entertainment. He joins social service and school activities, which teach leadership and responsibility. In this way, an ideal student prepares himself not only for examinations but also for a useful and honourable life. True excellence is the combination of knowledge, discipline, kindness, and the courage to keep improving every day.

Bangla Meaning of An Ideal Student Paragraph

আদর্শ ছাত্রের বাংলা অর্থ

একজন আদর্শ ছাত্র শিক্ষাকে শুধু নম্বরের প্রতিযোগিতা মনে করে না, বরং দায়িত্ব মনে করে। সে নিয়মিত ক্লাসে যায়, শিক্ষকের কথা মনোযোগ দিয়ে শোনে এবং না বুঝলে প্রশ্ন করে। সে প্রতিদিন পড়াশোনা করে, পাঠ ভুলে যাওয়ার আগেই ঝালিয়ে নেয় এবং না বুঝে মুখস্থ করার বদলে বিষয়টি বুঝতে চেষ্টা করে।

একজন আদর্শ ছাত্র চরিত্রেও ভালো হয়। সে বাবা-মা, শিক্ষক ও সহপাঠীদের সম্মান করে এবং স্কুলের নিয়ম মেনে চলে। সে সত্যবাদী, সময়নিষ্ঠ ও পরোপকারী হয় এবং নিজের ভুল স্বীকার করতে দ্বিধা করে না। ব্যায়াম, ঘুম ও খেলাধুলার মাধ্যমে সে শরীর সুস্থ রাখে, কারণ সুস্থ শরীর পড়ায় মনোযোগ বাড়ায়।

সাফল্যে সে অহংকারী হয় না, আবার ব্যর্থতায় হতাশও হয় না। সে দুর্বল সহপাঠীদের সাহায্য করে, নোট গুছিয়ে রাখে এবং সময়ের সঠিক ব্যবহার করে। এভাবেই একজন আদর্শ ছাত্র শুধু পরীক্ষার জন্য নয়, একটি সুন্দর ও উপকারী জীবনের জন্য নিজেকে তৈরি করে।

Important Word Meanings

English WordBangla Meaning
Responsibilityদায়িত্ব
Regularনিয়মিত
Attentiveমনোযোগী
Memoriseমুখস্থ করা
Punctualসময়নিষ্ঠ
Truthfulসত্যবাদী
Disciplineশৃঙ্খলা
Concentrationমনোযোগ
Organisedগোছানো
Citizenshipনাগরিকত্ব

Exam Tips

  • Choose the version that matches your class: 150 words for Class 6–7, 250 words for Class 8–10 and SSC, 300 words for SSC and HSC.
  • Do not memorise the whole paragraph word by word. Learn the main points — regularity, understanding, character, health, and facing failure — and write them in your own sentences.
  • Keep one paragraph in one block. Do not break it into many small paragraphs unless the question asks for it.
  • Use the Bangla meaning to understand difficult words before you memorise the English version.
  • Revise the paragraph once the night before the exam instead of reading it for the first time in the hall.

Tree Plantation

Tree plantation means deliberately growing trees in suitable places and caring for them. It is important in Bangladesh because trees provide oxygen, shade, fruit, wood, soil protection, and habitats for birds and other animals. Their roots help reduce erosion, while leaves cool the surroundings and improve air quality.

We can plant trees beside roads, around schools, near ponds, on unused land, and in home gardens. Fruit trees can provide food and income, while native shade trees benefit people and wildlife. A planting programme should select healthy saplings, prepare the soil, water them regularly, and protect them from grazing animals. Planting without later care often leads to failure.

People should stop unnecessary cutting and replace trees that must be removed. Schools and local groups can observe a tree-planting day, but caring for the saplings throughout the year is more important than a ceremony. By increasing green spaces and protecting old trees, we help the climate, soil, economy, and health of our communities. Every household and institution can contribute.

A publication made by a school community

A school magazine is a collection of writing and artwork prepared by students and teachers. It may appear once a year and include poems, essays, short stories, reports, drawings, puzzles, interviews, and records of important school events.

A teacher usually guides the editorial committee, while students collect submissions, edit drafts, arrange illustrations, and check proofs. The process teaches planning, cooperation, careful reading, and respect for other people’s ideas. A student who is quiet in class may discover confidence after seeing a poem or report printed in the magazine.

The publication also preserves the character of the school during a particular year. Readers can learn about achievements, clubs, celebrations, and community projects. A magazine should welcome different abilities rather than publish only perfect writing. With encouragement and honest editing, it becomes both a record of school life and a training ground for future communicators.

item.content:encoded:
A quiet morning in the cold season

A winter morning arrives slowly under a veil of mist. Before sunrise, trees and rooftops look blurred, and the familiar road seems shorter because the fog hides its far end. The air feels sharp, so people wrap themselves in shawls, sweaters, or blankets.

The scene changes when the sun rises. Golden light gradually burns away the mist, dew shines on grass, and birds begin to call from the branches. Farmers lead their cattle to the fields, while children hurry to school after warming themselves beside a small fire. Tea stalls become popular because a hot cup gives workers comfort before the day begins.

Winter mornings are especially pleasant to those who can enjoy them at leisure. Date juice, cakes, fresh vegetables, and warm sunshine are seasonal pleasures. Yet poor people often suffer because they lack warm clothing and shelter. We should share blankets and food with neighbours who need help.

A winter morning combines beauty, freshness, and hardship. Its peaceful atmosphere is memorable, but its human lesson is equally important: comfort should not make us forget the vulnerable.

Load Shedding

Load shedding is the planned interruption of electricity when demand is greater than the available supply or when the power network needs protection. It may also occur because of fuel shortages, damaged equipment, storms, or faults in transmission lines.

An unexpected power cut disturbs homes, schools, hospitals, shops, factories, and farms. Students cannot study comfortably, food may spoil in a refrigerator, water pumps may stop, and businesses can lose working hours. Hospitals need generators and careful planning because many patients depend on electrical equipment. Repeated cuts can also damage appliances when the current returns suddenly.

The problem can be reduced by producing sufficient electricity, repairing the grid, preventing illegal connections, and using renewable sources such as solar power. Consumers should switch off unnecessary lights and fans, use energy-efficient appliances, and avoid wasting electricity during peak periods. Authorities should publish reliable schedules and give priority to essential services. Responsible use by citizens, combined with investment in generation and distribution, can make the supply more dependable.

item.title: How to Write an Application: Format, Examples & Tips
item.author: Study Koro
item.description: Application writing is an important part of English writing in Bangladesh. Students may need to write an application to the headmaster, principal, department
item.content:encoded:
Application writing is an important part of English writing in Bangladesh. Students may need to write an application to the headmaster, principal, department head, or another authority for different reasons.

For example, you may need to write an application for leave, a testimonial, a transfer certificate, permission for a study tour, or another school or college matter. University students and job seekers also write formal applications for academic and professional purposes.

The good news is that most formal applications follow a simple structure. Once you understand the format, you can write an application for almost any situation.

This guide explains the basic application writing format and provides examples for school, college, university, and job applications.

What Is an Application?

An application is a formal written request made to a person or authority.

For example:

  • A student writes to the headmaster for leave.
  • A student writes to the principal for a testimonial.
  • A university student writes to the examination office for a transcript.
  • A student writes to an authority for permission to join a study tour.
  • A job seeker writes to an employer to apply for a position.

The purpose of an application should be clear from the beginning. Avoid unnecessary information and explain exactly what you are requesting.

Basic Application Writing Format

A formal application usually contains these parts:

  1. Date
  2. Name and designation of the recipient
  3. Institution or organisation
  4. Address
  5. Subject
  6. Salutation
  7. Main body
  8. Closing
  9. Name and identifying information of the applicant

A simple structure looks like this:

Date

The [Designation] [Institution Name] [Address]

Subject: Application for [purpose].

Sir/Madam,

First paragraph: Introduce yourself and explain why you are writing.

Second paragraph: Give the necessary details about your situation.

Final paragraph: Clearly state what you are requesting.

Yours faithfully/obediently, [Your Name] [Class/Department] [Roll/ID]

The exact format can vary between institutions, so students should follow any specific instructions given by their school, college, university, or employer.

1. Application for Leave

A leave application is written when you need permission to remain absent from school, college, or another institution.

Example: Leave Application for Illness

15 January 2026

The Headmaster Ideal High School Motijheel, Dhaka

Subject: Application for leave of absence.

Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I am a student of Class IX, Section B, of your school. I have been suffering from a high fever for the last three days, and the doctor has advised me to take rest.

For this reason, I will not be able to attend school from 15 January to 18 January 2026. I therefore request you to kindly grant me leave for these four days.

I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours obediently, Md. Rakib Hasan Class IX, Section B Roll No. 17

What to include in a leave application

Make sure you mention:

  • The reason for your absence
  • The dates of your leave
  • Your class or department
  • Your roll or student ID
  • Any supporting document if the institution requires one

Do not write a long explanation. Give only the information the authority needs.

For a ready-made example, see our Application for Leave of Absence: Class 6 to 12 Students.

2. Application for a Testimonial

A testimonial is an official document that may provide information about a student's academic record, conduct, or period of study at an institution.

Students may need a testimonial after completing SSC or HSC or when applying for further education or other purposes.

Example: Testimonial Application

10 February 2026

The Principal Dhaka College New Market, Dhaka

Subject: Application for a testimonial.

Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I passed the HSC examination in 2025 from your college under the Dhaka Education Board. I am now preparing to apply for higher studies and require a testimonial from the college.

I therefore request you to kindly issue me a testimonial at your earliest convenience. I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours obediently, Sumaiya Akter HSC 2025, Science Group Roll No. 124356

Tip for students

If the institution has a specific testimonial form, use that form instead of writing a separate application. Some Bangladeshi institutions provide their own testimonial forms with fields for student information and academic details.

You can also read a full example in our Application for Testimonial For Class 6, 7, 8, SSC and HSC.

3. Application for an Academic Transcript

University students may need an academic transcript when applying for higher studies, scholarships, employment, or other official purposes.

The procedure is different from one university to another. Some universities require a specific form, fee payment, clearance, or supporting documents.

Example

22 March 2026

The Controller of Examinations University of Dhaka Dhaka-1000

Subject: Application for issuance of academic transcript.

Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I completed my Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science and Engineering from your university in 2025. I now require an official academic transcript for my application for higher studies abroad.

I have completed the required payment and attached the necessary documents with this application.

I therefore request you to kindly issue two copies of my official academic transcript.

Yours faithfully, Mohammad Tanvir Ahmed Registration No. 2021-715-001 Session: 2020–2021 Department of CSE

Important

Before submitting a university application, check your university's current instructions. Do not assume that every university uses the same process.

4. Application for a Transfer Certificate

A transfer certificate application is generally written when a student needs official permission or documentation to leave one institution and continue studies elsewhere.

Example

20 April 2026

The Principal ABC College Dhaka

Subject: Application for a transfer certificate.

Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I am a student of Class XII of your college. My family is moving to another city, and I need to continue my studies there.

I therefore request you to kindly issue me a transfer certificate so that I can complete the necessary admission formalities at another institution.

I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours obediently, Rahim Ahmed Class XII Roll No. 25 Science Group

For another full example, see our Application for Transfer Certificate.

5. Application for Permission to Join a Study Tour

Students may need permission from their school or college authority before joining an educational tour or study tour.

Example

5 May 2026

The Headmaster ABC High School Dhaka

Subject: Application for permission to join a study tour.

Sir,

With due respect, we, the students of Class X, would like to arrange an educational study tour to the National Museum in Dhaka. Such a visit would give us an opportunity to learn more about the history and culture of Bangladesh outside the classroom.

We therefore request you to kindly grant us permission to arrange the study tour under the guidance of our teachers.

We shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours obediently, The students of Class X ABC High School Dhaka

Tip

For a group application, write on behalf of the students and clearly mention the proposed destination, purpose, and supervision arrangements when relevant.

6. Job Application Letter

A job application is different from a school application. Instead of asking a school authority for permission or a document, you are introducing yourself to an employer and explaining why you are suitable for a particular position.

A modern job application should be concise and specific.

Example

5 April 2026

The Head of Human Resources ABC Bank Limited Gulshan, Dhaka

Subject: Application for the position of Management Trainee Officer.

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to apply for the position of Management Trainee Officer advertised on your company's website.

I recently completed my BBA in Finance from North South University with a CGPA of 3.78. During my undergraduate studies, I completed a three-month internship with a commercial bank, where I gained practical experience in credit analysis and customer service.

I believe my academic background, internship experience, and communication skills would allow me to contribute effectively to your organisation. My CV and relevant academic documents are attached for your consideration.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my qualifications in an interview.

Yours faithfully, Nusrat Jahan nusrat.jahan@example.com +880 1XXX-XXXXXX

Job application tip

Do not copy the same application for every job.

Mention the actual position, organisation, and skills that are relevant to the job. Your application should support your CV rather than repeat everything in it.

7. Application for a Character Certificate

A character certificate or similar official document may be requested for admission, employment, or other purposes.

The exact name and procedure can vary by institution.

Example

12 June 2026

The Headmaster ABC High School Dhaka

Subject: Application for a character certificate.

Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I was a student of your school and passed the SSC examination in 2026. I now require a character certificate for my further studies.

I therefore request you to kindly issue me a character certificate mentioning my conduct and period of study at the institution.

I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours obediently, Sadia Islam SSC 2026 Roll No. 123456

How to Write an Application Step by Step

If you have never written a formal application before, follow these steps.

Step 1: Identify the person you are writing to

Find out who should receive the application.

For example:

  • The Headmaster
  • The Principal
  • The Head of the Department
  • The Controller of Examinations
  • The Human Resources Manager

Use the correct designation.

Step 2: Write a clear subject

The subject should tell the reader what you want.

Good examples:

  • Application for leave of absence
  • Application for a testimonial
  • Application for issuance of an academic transcript
  • Application for a transfer certificate
  • Application for permission to join a study tour

Do not write a long subject.

Step 3: Introduce yourself

Tell the reader who you are.

For example:

I am a student of Class X, Section A, of your school.

A university student could write:

I am a student of the Department of Computer Science and Engineering.

Step 4: Explain the reason

Give the important facts related to your request.

For a leave application, mention the reason and dates.

For a testimonial, explain why you need it.

For a transcript, explain what you need and, if relevant, what the transcript is for.

Step 5: Make your request clearly

Do not make the reader guess what you want.

For example:

I therefore request you to kindly grant me leave for three days.

Step 6: End politely

Use an appropriate formal closing.

For example:

I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Then add your name and relevant identification details.

Common Mistakes in Application Writing

Students often make simple mistakes that can make an application look careless.

1. Forgetting the subject

The subject helps the reader understand the purpose of the application quickly.

2. Writing too much

A formal application should contain the information necessary to understand and process the request. Avoid unrelated stories.

3. Using informal language

Avoid expressions such as:

  • Hi Sir
  • What's up
  • I wanna request
  • Please help me out
  • Thanks a lot

Use polite and formal language instead.

4. Using unnecessary difficult words

You do not need complicated English to write a good application.

For example:

I would like to request you to kindly grant me leave.

is clear and sufficient.

A simple sentence is usually better than a long sentence filled with difficult words.

5. Forgetting personal details

For school and college applications, include the details needed to identify you, such as:

  • Name
  • Class
  • Section
  • Roll number
  • Registration number
  • Department
  • Student ID

Only include information that is relevant to the application.

6. Using the wrong closing

Choose the closing according to the situation and the style required by your institution.

For traditional school applications, “Yours obediently” is commonly used. For professional applications, “Yours faithfully” or “Yours sincerely” may be more appropriate depending on how you address the recipient.

Yours Obediently, Yours Faithfully, or Yours Sincerely?

These expressions are often confusing for students.

Yours obediently

This is commonly found in traditional school and college applications addressed to teachers or institutional authorities.

Yours faithfully

This is commonly used in formal correspondence when you do not address the recipient by name, especially in British-style business writing.

Example:

Dear Sir/Madam, Yours faithfully,

Yours sincerely

This is commonly used when you address the recipient by name.

Example:

Dear Mr Karim, Yours sincerely,

However, institutions may have their own preferred format. If your school or university gives you a prescribed format, follow it.

Application Writing Format for SSC and HSC Students

For SSC and HSC students, application writing is also an important part of English writing practice.

Common topics include:

  • Application for leave
  • Application for a testimonial
  • Application for a transfer certificate
  • Application for a seat in the school hostel
  • Application for permission to arrange a study tour
  • Application for setting up a canteen
  • Application for improving library facilities
  • Application for arranging a cultural programme

For examination practice, first understand the format. Then practise writing different applications instead of memorising one answer word for word.

A memorised application may not fit a new question exactly.

Application Writing vs. Formal Letter Writing

These two types of writing are related, but they have different purposes.

An application is usually a formal request made to an authority.

A formal letter can have a wider purpose, such as making a complaint, requesting information, giving notice, or communicating with an organisation.

For example:

Application: Application to the principal for leave.

Formal letter: Letter to the editor about traffic congestion in Dhaka.

Knowing the purpose helps you choose the right format.

If you need to practise formal letter writing, read our Letter How to improve English for a complete example.

Quick Application Writing Template

You can use this template when you need to write a new application.

[Date]

The [Designation] [Institution Name] [Address]

Subject: Application for [purpose].

Sir/Madam,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I am [your position/class/department].

[Explain the reason for your application and provide the important details.]

I therefore request you to kindly [clearly state what you want].

I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours faithfully/obediently, [Your Name] [Class/Department] [Roll/Student ID]

Use this as a framework, not as a paragraph to memorise. Change the details and sentences according to the situation.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the format of an application in Bangladesh?

A formal application generally includes the date, recipient's designation and institution, subject, salutation, body, closing, and the applicant's identifying details. The exact format may vary depending on the institution.

How do I start an application?

Start by identifying the recipient and writing a clear subject. In the first paragraph, introduce yourself and explain the reason for writing.

How long should a formal application be?

For most school and college applications, one or two short paragraphs are enough. Include the necessary information without adding unrelated details.

Should I write an application by hand?

Follow the instructions of the institution or organisation. Some schools may prefer handwritten applications, while universities and employers may require typed or online submissions.

What paper size should I use?

If the institution has not specified a paper size, A4 is a practical choice for a typed formal document. However, always follow the instructions provided by the receiving institution.

Can I use the same application format for every topic?

You can use the same basic structure, but the content should change according to your purpose. A leave application, testimonial application, university transcript request, and job application should not contain the same body text.

Should I memorise application examples for exams?

It is better to understand the format and practise different topics. Memorising complete applications can make it difficult to answer questions that use a different situation.

Final Tips for Writing a Good Application

Before submitting your application, check these points:

  • Is the recipient correct?
  • Is the subject clear?
  • Did you explain the reason?
  • Did you make your request clear?
  • Did you include your class, roll, ID, or department where necessary?
  • Did you use polite and formal language?
  • Did you check spelling and grammar?
  • Did you follow any instructions given by the institution?
  • Did you remove unnecessary information?

A good application does not need complicated English. It needs a clear purpose, correct information, polite language, and a suitable format.

Once you understand the basic structure, you can write applications for school, college, university, and professional situations with much more confidence.

When the air becomes unsafe

Air pollution occurs when smoke, dust, poisonous gases, or tiny particles enter the atmosphere in harmful amounts. Vehicle exhaust, brick kilns, factories, burning rubbish, construction work, and forest fires are common sources. In crowded cities, pollution can become especially serious when wind is weak.

Breathing polluted air may irritate the eyes and throat and can worsen asthma, heart disease, and other respiratory problems. Children, older people, and outdoor workers are often most vulnerable. Pollution also damages crops, buildings, animals, and the climate.

The solution requires both public policy and personal responsibility. Authorities can enforce emission standards, improve public transport, control construction dust, and promote clean energy. Citizens can avoid burning waste, maintain vehicles, plant suitable trees, and walk or share transport when possible. Schools can teach children to notice local pollution and support clean-air campaigns. Protecting the atmosphere is a shared duty because everyone depends on healthy air.

My favourite hobby is gardening. I grow flowers, herbs, and a few vegetables in pots and in a small patch beside our home. I loosen the soil, sow seeds, water the plants, and remove weeds. Watching a seed become a living plant teaches me patience and care.

Gardening refreshes me after study and gives me gentle exercise. Green plants make the surroundings cooler and more attractive, while herbs and vegetables can provide fresh food. I reuse kitchen containers as planters and avoid wasting water. Sometimes I share seedlings with my neighbours. This hobby has made me more interested in nature and more aware that healthy surroundings depend on daily responsibility. I also keep a small diary where I write the names of new plants and note when I sowed their seeds. This diary helps me remember what worked and what did not.

Beginning the day with purpose

Early rising means waking at a regular time that allows a person to begin the day without haste. The quiet hours can be used for prayer, exercise, reading, revision, or planning. Fresh air and fewer distractions often make the morning feel especially productive.

The habit is helpful only when it follows adequate sleep. A student who stays awake late and wakes before resting properly will be tired, not successful. A fixed bedtime, limited screen use at night, and preparation of school materials can make morning rising easier.

People have different routines, so no single clock time suits everyone. What matters is a balanced schedule that includes sleep, study, work, meals, and recreation. A calm beginning can improve punctuality and concentration, but health should never be sacrificed merely to claim that one rises early.

The consequences of cutting forests

Trees are being removed for fuel, timber, roads, farms, and construction. When this clearing continues without replanting, the result is deforestation. It destroys animal habitats, weakens soil, reduces rainfall absorption, and adds to global warming because fewer trees remain to take in carbon dioxide.

Deforested land is more likely to suffer erosion, floods, drought, and extreme heat. People who depend on forests for food, medicine, or work also lose important resources. The damage can continue for many years after the last tree is cut.

We should protect natural forests, enforce laws against illegal logging, and restore damaged land with suitable species. Schools and families can plant and care for trees, reduce wasteful paper use, and teach others why forests matter. Conservation is a shared duty because healthy forests support a healthy society.

Eve Teasing Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

"Eve-teasing" is a common term for unwanted comments, gestures, following, staring, or other harassment directed at girls and women. It is not harmless fun. It creates fear, restricts movement, interrupts education, and denies a person the right to travel safely.

Families and schools should teach respect, equality, consent, and responsible conduct from an early age. Witnesses can support the victim, seek help from trusted adults or authorities, and avoid blaming the person who was harassed. Communities need safe transport, lighting, complaint systems, and prompt enforcement of the law. Public spaces become safer when every person rejects harassment and protects the dignity of others. Boys and men must understand that silence and peer approval can encourage abuse, and that real respect means speaking up against it. A girl should never be told to change her education, clothing, or dreams to suit someone else's misconduct.

Physical Exercise

Physical exercise is the movement of the body in a planned and healthy way. Walking, swimming, cycling, running, gardening, games, and sports can all keep us active. Exercise makes muscles stronger, improves blood circulation, supports a healthy weight, and helps the mind remain fresh.

A young and fit person may choose a sport or a brisk run, while an elderly or weak person can begin with gentle walking and stretching. No single activity is suitable for everyone. It is wise to warm up, practise regularly, drink water, and stop if the body feels unwell. Good food and sufficient sleep are also necessary for health.

Exercise teaches discipline as well as fitness. A student who takes a short walk or plays outdoors often returns to study with better concentration. Many activities are free, so lack of money need not prevent a healthy routine. We should avoid sitting for long hours and make movement part of everyday life. Good health supports work, study, and happiness, making physical exercise an important habit for people of every age.

Gender Discrimination Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

Gender discrimination means treating people differently because they are male or female. It can appear at home, in school, at work, or in public life. For example, a girl may be discouraged from studying, while a boy may be excused from household duties. Such attitudes prevent families and nations from using the abilities of all their citizens.

Everyone deserves equal respect, education, safety, and a fair chance to work. Parents should give sons and daughters the same encouragement, and schools should challenge unfair stereotypes. Laws can protect equal rights, but lasting change also depends on everyday behaviour. When women and men share responsibilities and opportunities, families become stronger and society makes better progress. Teachers should also give girls and boys equal chances in class, in sports, and in leadership roles at school. Equal treatment in small things builds equal respect in big things.

Gender Discrimination Paragraph in 250 Words

Best for Class 8–10 and SSC.

Gender discrimination means treating people differently because they are male or female. It can appear at home, in school, at work, or in public life. For example, a girl may be discouraged from studying, while a boy may be excused from household duties. A woman may be paid less for the same work, or a man may be laughed at for choosing a job that people call a woman's job. Such attitudes prevent families and nations from using the abilities of all their citizens.

Everyone deserves equal respect, education, safety, and a fair chance to work. A girl has the same right as a boy to go to school, to choose a subject she likes, and to dream of a career. Parents should give sons and daughters the same encouragement, and teachers should praise ability, not gender. Schools should challenge unfair stereotypes in books, stories, and everyday talk.

Laws can protect equal rights, but lasting change also depends on everyday behaviour. Boys should learn to share household work, and girls should be given confidence to speak and lead. When women and men share responsibilities and opportunities, families become stronger and society makes better progress. A country cannot move forward if half of its people are held back. In many families, parents still spend more on a son's education than on a daughter's, and this unfair habit must change if society wants real progress. Both sons and daughters can bring honour to a family.

When women and men share responsibilities and opportunities, families become stronger and society makes better progress. A country cannot move forward if half of its people are held back, because talent is not limited to one gender. The media also has a role to play, because films, advertisements, and stories that show women as weak or men as careless only strengthen old stereotypes. Fair stories build a fair society.

A changing climate and our responsibility

The climate is changing because large amounts of heat-trapping gases are entering the atmosphere. Vehicles, factories, power stations, and the destruction of forests all contribute to this increase. A warmer planet can bring irregular rain, longer heat waves, melting ice, stronger storms, and rising sea levels.

These effects are serious for Bangladesh. Floods and cyclones can damage homes and crops, while salt water may enter fields and drinking-water sources. Poor families usually suffer most because they have fewer resources to rebuild.

We cannot solve the problem through one action. Public authorities should protect forests, develop clean energy, improve warning systems, and plan climate-resilient towns. Citizens can conserve electricity, plant and protect trees, reduce waste, and use buses or bicycles when practical. Education is important because informed people make better choices.

Climate change is not a distant issue. Careful decisions today can reduce future damage and protect the lives and livelihoods of coming generations.

Price Hike

A price hike is a sustained increase in the cost of everyday goods and services. When rice, vegetables, fuel, medicine, rent, or transport becomes more expensive, families must spend more for the same standard of living. The burden is especially heavy for workers whose salaries do not rise with the market.

Prices may increase because of inflation, higher fuel and production costs, floods or other disasters, shortages, currency changes, transport problems, hoarding, and excessive profit-taking. A disruption in one part of the supply chain can affect the final price in a shop. The result can be anxiety, reduced nutrition, postponed treatment, and greater poverty.

The government can respond by ensuring adequate supply, improving storage and transport, monitoring markets, taking action against illegal hoarding, and assisting families in genuine difficulty. Farmers and small traders also need fair access to finance and markets. Consumers should compare prices, avoid waste, and not create artificial shortages by panic buying. A coordinated effort can protect both producers and buyers while the economy stabilises.

Metro Rail Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

Metro rail is a rapid urban transport system in which electric trains travel along dedicated tracks, often above busy roads. It can carry large numbers of passengers quickly and reduce pressure on crowded streets. In a growing city, a dependable metro service saves commuting time, lowers fuel use, and can reduce air pollution and traffic noise.

Dhaka's first metro line, MRT Line 6, runs from Uttara North to Motijheel. Its first section, Uttara North to Agargaon, opened on 28 December 2022, and the Agargaon to Motijheel section opened on 4 November 2023. Passengers should queue, buy the correct ticket, keep stations clean, and offer priority seats to those who need them. With responsible use and careful expansion, metro rail can make urban travel cleaner and more efficient. Passengers should queue, buy the correct ticket, keep stations clean, and offer priority seats to those who need them. Safety rules must be followed near platforms and doors. Metro rail alone cannot solve every transport problem; buses, walking routes, cycling facilities, and good planning are also necessary. With responsible use and careful expansion, it can make urban travel cleaner and more efficient. Students and office workers now reach their destinations on time, and many families have moved closer to metro stations to enjoy this benefit. Clean stations and polite behaviour make the journey pleasant for all.

International Mother Language Day Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

International Mother Language Day is observed on 21 February to honour the languages spoken by people around the world. The day also recalls the language movement in Bangladesh, when students and citizens protested in 1952 for the right to use Bangla. Several demonstrators lost their lives, and their sacrifice became a lasting symbol of linguistic rights.

People mark the day by visiting Shaheed Minar, placing flowers, arranging discussions, holding cultural programmes, and reading poetry. The observance reminds us that language carries history, identity, and knowledge. We should respect our mother tongue, develop it through reading and writing, and show equal respect for other languages. Protecting linguistic diversity helps communities live with dignity and understanding. On 17 November 1999, UNESCO proclaimed 21 February as International Mother Language Day, and it has been observed around the world since 2000. This honour came because of the sacrifice of 1952.

International Mother Language Day Paragraph in 250 Words

Best for Class 8–10 and SSC.

International Mother Language Day is observed on 21 February to honour the languages spoken by people around the world. The day also recalls the language movement in Bangladesh, when students and citizens protested in 1952 for the right to use Bangla as a state language. On 21 February 1952, police opened fire on a peaceful student procession in Dhaka. Salam, Barkat, Rafiq, Jabbar, and Shafiur Rahman were killed, and their sacrifice became a lasting symbol of linguistic rights. Their memory is honoured at the Shaheed Minar, the Martyrs' Monument in Dhaka.

Years later, the world recognised this sacrifice. On 17 November 1999, UNESCO proclaimed 21 February as International Mother Language Day, and it has been observed around the world since 2000. People mark the day by visiting Shaheed Minar, placing flowers, arranging discussions, holding cultural programmes, and reading poetry. The observance reminds us that language carries history, identity, and knowledge. We should respect our mother tongue, develop it through reading and writing, and show equal respect for other languages. Protecting linguistic diversity helps communities live with dignity and understanding. In Bangladesh, the day begins in the early hours, when people walk barefoot to the Shaheed Minar with flowers in their hands. They sing 'Amar Bhaiyer Rokte Rangano Ekushey February', the song written in memory of the martyrs, and the whole nation remembers the price paid for Bangla. The day teaches us that a mother tongue is not only a means of communication; it is the voice of a people's history, poetry, and dreams.

International Mother Language Day Paragraph in 300 Words

Best for SSC and HSC.

International Mother Language Day is observed on 21 February to honour the languages spoken by people around the world. The day also recalls the language movement in Bangladesh, when students and citizens protested in 1952 for the right to use Bangla as a state language. At that time, most people of the country spoke Bangla, yet the central government had declared that Urdu alone would be the state language. On 21 February 1952, students of the University of Dhaka defied a ban on public gatherings and marched to demand recognition for Bangla. Near Dhaka Medical College, police opened fire on the peaceful procession. Salam, Barkat, Rafiq, Jabbar, and Shafiur Rahman were killed, and many others were injured. Their sacrifice became a lasting symbol of linguistic rights, and within a few years Bangla was recognised as an official language.

Years later, the world recognised this sacrifice. On 17 November 1999, UNESCO proclaimed 21 February as International Mother Language Day, and it has been observed around the world since 2000. People mark the day by visiting Shaheed Minar, placing flowers, arranging discussions, holding cultural programmes, and reading poetry. The observance reminds us that language carries history, identity, and knowledge. We should respect our mother tongue, develop it through reading and writing, and show equal respect for other languages. Protecting linguistic diversity helps communities live with dignity and understanding. Students who protested in 1952 showed that a people who love their language will also defend their dignity. Today, when we speak Bangla freely, we should remember that this freedom was bought with blood. The best way to honour the martyrs is to use Bangla correctly, to read Bangla books, and to teach our children to love their mother tongue while respecting every other language of the world.

আন্তর্জাতিক মাতৃভাষা দিবস অনুচ্ছেদের বাংলা অর্থ

আন্তর্জাতিক মাতৃভাষা দিবস প্রতি বছর ২১ ফেব্রুয়ারি পালিত হয়, বিশ্বের সব মানুষের ভাষাকে সম্মান জানাতে। এই দিনটি বাংলাদেশের ভাষা আন্দোলনকেও স্মরণ করিয়ে দেয়, যখন ১৯৫২ সালে ছাত্র ও সাধারণ মানুষ বাংলাকে রাষ্ট্রভাষা করার দাবিতে আন্দোলন করেছিল। ১৯৫২ সালের ২১ ফেব্রুয়ারি ঢাকায় শান্তিপূর্ণ মিছিলে পুলিশ গুলি চালায়। সালাম, বরকত, রফিক, জব্বার ও শফিউর রহমান শহীদ হন এবং তাঁদের আত্মত্যাগ ভাষার অধিকারের চিরন্তন প্রতীক হয়ে ওঠে।

বহু বছর পর বিশ্ব এই আত্মত্যাগকে স্বীকৃতি দেয়। ১৯৯৯ সালের ১৭ নভেম্বর ইউনেস্কো ২১ ফেব্রুয়ারিকে আন্তর্জাতিক মাতৃভাষা দিবস হিসেবে ঘোষণা করে এবং ২০০০ সাল থেকে সারা বিশ্বে এটি পালিত হচ্ছে। এই দিনে মানুষ শহীদ মিনারে ফুল দেয়, আলোচনা সভা ও সাংস্কৃতিক অনুষ্ঠান করে এবং কবিতা পাঠ করে। ভাষা ইতিহাস, পরিচয় ও জ্ঞান বহন করে — তাই মাতৃভাষাকে সম্মান করা এবং অন্য ভাষাকেও সমান সম্মান দেওয়া আমাদের কর্তব্য।

This is the completing story of a lion and a mouse, written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The given beginning is: "Once, a lion was sleeping under a tree in a forest. A little mouse came out of its hole and began to run over the lion's body." Read the complete story below, then learn the moral, the Bangla meaning and the important words at the end.

A Lion and a Mouse (Complete Story)

Once, a lion was sleeping under a tree in a forest. A little mouse came out of its hole and began to run over the lion's body. The mouse was playing happily and did not notice that the lion had woken up. Suddenly, the lion caught the little creature with his strong paw and prepared to punish it.

The mouse was very frightened. It begged for freedom in a trembling voice. "Please let me go, O King," it said. "I am very small, and I am not good food for you. If you spare my life, I may be able to help you someday."

The lion laughed at the unlikely idea. How could such a small creature help the king of the forest? But the mouse looked so helpless that the lion felt pity. He opened his paw and let the mouse go. "Run away," he said, "and do not disturb my sleep again."

The mouse thanked the lion again and again and ran back to its hole. The lion soon forgot the whole matter and went back to sleep.

Days passed, and the forest returned to its usual calm. The lion hunted, rested, and walked through his territory without fear. He did not remember the small mouse at all. But the mouse remembered the lion's kindness and often told its family how the king of the forest had spared its life.

Some time later, hunters came to the forest and set a strong net to catch the lion. That night, the lion walked into the trap. The ropes held him fast, and he could not free himself. He roared loudly in anger and fear, and his roar was heard far away.

The little mouse heard the roar and hurried to the place. It saw the lion caught in the net and remembered the lion's kindness. Without wasting time, it began to gnaw through the ropes with its sharp teeth, one strand at a time. The work was slow, but the mouse did not stop. At last, the net was cut, and the lion was free.

The lion thanked the mouse warmly. He understood that size does not determine usefulness. Everyone has abilities that may become valuable in an unexpected situation. Kindness also creates bonds that return when help is needed. From that day, the lion and the mouse became good friends.

Moral

Never despise a small friend; kindness is rarely wasted.

Bangla Meaning of the Story

গল্পটির বাংলা অর্থ

একদিন একটি সিংহ বনের একটি গাছের নিচে ঘুমাচ্ছিল। একটি ছোট ইঁদুর তার গর্ত থেকে বের হয়ে সিংহের শরীরের উপর দৌড়াতে লাগল। সিংহ জেগে উঠে ইঁদুরটিকে ধরে ফেলল। ইঁদুর ভয়ে কাঁপতে কাঁপতে প্রাণভিক্ষা চাইল এবং বলল, একদিন হয়তো সে সিংহের উপকারে আসতে পারবে।

সিংহ হাসলেও দয়া করে ইঁদুরটিকে ছেড়ে দিল। কিছুদিন পর শিকারিরা সিংহকে শক্ত জালে আটকে ফেলল। সিংহের গর্জন শুনে ইঁদুর ছুটে এলো এবং তার ধারালো দাঁত দিয়ে একটু একটু করে জালের দড়ি কেটে সিংহকে মুক্ত করল। তখন সিংহ বুঝল, ছোট বলে কাউকে তুচ্ছ করা উচিত নয়। দয়া কখনো বৃথা যায় না।

এরপর বনে আবার শান্তি ফিরে এলো। সিংহ শিকার করত, বিশ্রাম নিত এবং নির্ভয়ে ঘুরে বেড়াত। সে ছোট ইঁদুরের কথা ভুলেই গিয়েছিল। কিন্তু ইঁদুর সিংহের দয়া ভোলেনি এবং প্রায়ই তার পরিবারকে বলত, বনের রাজা কীভাবে তার প্রাণ রক্ষা করেছিলেন।

Important Word Meanings

English WordBangla Meaning
Creatureপ্রাণী
Tremblingকাঁপতে থাকা
Spareরেহাই দেওয়া
Pityদয়া, করুণা
Trapফাঁদ
Roarগর্জন
Gnawকুটকুট করে কাটা
Strandসুতো, দড়ির অংশ
Despiseতুচ্ছ করা, ঘৃণা করা
Unexpectedঅপ্রত্যাশিত

Exam Tips

  • Begin the story with the given beginning exactly as it is written in the question, then continue it in your own words.
  • Keep the events in order: the lion catches the mouse, the mouse begs for freedom, the lion frees it, the hunters trap the lion, and the mouse cuts the net.
  • Write in the past tense, because the story happened in the past.
  • Do not change the main idea of the story. The mouse must save the lion by its own small ability.
  • End the story with the moral in a separate short paragraph, as shown above.
  • Use the lion's and the mouse's feelings in your sentences. Words like frightened, pity and grateful make the story lively.

item.content:encoded:
On this page you will find a letter about how to improve English, written in simple English for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. It gives the format of a personal letter, a full example letter, its Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. You can learn the letter for your examination and also follow its advice to improve your English at the same time.

Format

  • Your address at the top of the letter, on the right or left side as your teacher advises.
  • The date below your address, so the reader knows when you wrote the letter.
  • A greeting or salutation, such as "Dear Tuhin," to the friend you are writing to.
  • The body of the letter, in three or four short paragraphs, with your main ideas in order.
  • A closing line, such as "With love," followed by your name at the end of the letter.
  • Simple and correct English throughout, with short sentences that are easy to understand.

Letter: How to Improve English (Example)

Dear Tuhin,

I hope you are well. Thank you for your letter. You asked me how I am improving my English, so I am writing to share the simple methods that are helping me most. English is important for our studies, for good jobs and for learning about the world, so I try to practise it a little every day instead of studying it only before an examination.

First, I read something in English every day. I read a short story, a newspaper article or a lesson from my textbook, and I note down useful expressions, not only single words. Then I listen to clear English conversations and repeat the sentences aloud, so my pronunciation and speaking become better. I also speak in English with a friend for a few minutes every day, even if I make mistakes.

Second, I write a little every day. I write a diary entry or a short paragraph, and then I check the spelling and grammar carefully. I keep a vocabulary notebook and try to use each new word in a sentence of my own, because a word is easy to remember when I use it myself. I use a dictionary when I do not know a word, but I do not memorise long lists without understanding them. When I make a mistake, I correct it and try again, because correction is a natural part of learning.

I hope these ideas will help you too. Start with fifteen minutes a day, and increase the time slowly when you feel comfortable. With patience and regular practice, your reading, writing, listening and speaking will all become stronger. Please write back soon and tell me how your practice is going.

With love,
Mim

Bangla Meaning

ইংরেজি উন্নত করার চিঠির বাংলা অর্থ

প্রিয় তুহিন, আশা করি তুমি ভালো আছো। তোমার চিঠির জন্য ধন্যবাদ। তুমি জানতে চেয়েছ আমি কীভাবে আমার ইংরেজি উন্নত করছি, তাই আমার সবচেয়ে কাজে লাগা সহজ উপায়গুলো জানিয়ে লিখছি। পড়াশোনা, ভালো চাকরি এবং পৃথিবী সম্পর্কে জানার জন্য ইংরেজি খুব গুরুত্বপূর্ণ। তাই আমি শুধু পরীক্ষার আগে নয়, প্রতিদিন একটু একটু করে ইংরেজি চর্চা করার চেষ্টা করি।

প্রথমে আমি প্রতিদিন ইংরেজিতে কিছু পড়ি। আমি একটি ছোট গল্প, সংবাদপত্রের একটি প্রবন্ধ অথবা পাঠ্যবইয়ের একটি পাঠ পড়ি এবং শুধু আলাদা আলাদা শব্দ নয়, কাজের বাক্যাংশগুলো লিখে রাখি। তারপর আমি পরিষ্কার ইংরেজি কথোপকথন শুনি এবং বাক্যগুলো জোরে জোরে বলি, যাতে আমার উচ্চারণ ও কথা বলা ভালো হয়। আমি প্রতিদিন কয়েক মিনিট একজন বন্ধুর সঙ্গে ইংরেজিতে কথা বলি, ভুল হলেও থামি না।

দ্বিতীয়ত, আমি প্রতিদিন একটু লিখি। আমি একটি ডায়েরি লিখি অথবা একটি ছোট অনুচ্ছেদ লিখি, তারপর বানান ও ব্যাকরণ ভালোভাবে দেখে নিই। আমি একটি শব্দভান্ডারের খাতা রাখি এবং প্রতিটি নতুন শব্দ নিজের বাক্যে ব্যবহার করার চেষ্টা করি, কারণ নিজে ব্যবহার করলে শব্দ মনে রাখা সহজ হয়। অজানা শব্দের জন্য আমি অভিধান ব্যবহার করি, কিন্তু না বুঝে লম্বা তালিকা মুখস্থ করি না। ভুল করলে তা ঠিক করে আবার চেষ্টা করি, কারণ ভুল থেকে শেখা শেখারই একটি স্বাভাবিক অংশ।

আশা করি এই ধারণাগুলো তোমারও কাজে আসবে। প্রতিদিন পনেরো মিনিট দিয়ে শুরু করো এবং স্বাচ্ছন্দ্য বোধ করলে ধীরে ধীরে সময় বাড়াও। ধৈর্য ও নিয়মিত চর্চায় তোমার পড়া, লেখা, শোনা ও বলা—সবই শক্তিশালী হবে। শীঘ্রই উত্তর লিখে জানিও তোমার চর্চা কেমন চলছে।

Important Word Meanings

English WordBangla Meaning
Improveউন্নত করা
Regularনিয়মিত
Expressionবাক্যাংশ
Pronunciationউচ্চারণ
Confidenceআত্মবিশ্বাস
Vocabularyশব্দভান্ডার
Dictionaryঅভিধান
Memoriseমুখস্থ করা
Embarrassedলজ্জিত
Patienceধৈর্য

Exam Tips

  • Learn the format first: address, date, salutation, body in three or four paragraphs, and a closing line with your name. Marks are given for a correct format as well as for good English.
  • Do not memorise the whole letter word by word. Learn the main points — reading daily, listening and speaking, writing daily, and using new words — and write them in your own simple sentences in the examination hall.
  • Keep your sentences short and correct. One long and confusing sentence is worse than two short and clear sentences, and short sentences are easier to write without grammar mistakes.
  • Use the Bangla meaning to understand the letter fully before you memorise the English version, so you can change a sentence in your own words if you forget the exact wording.
  • Revise the letter once the night before the examination and read it again in the morning, instead of trying to learn it for the first time in the hall.
